rules.title: Admin Share Access Followed by Remote Process Creation
rules.description: Correlates an ADMIN$ share access (Event 5145) with a process creation (4688) or service install (7045) on the same host within 10 minutes. This shows the classic copy-then-execute lateral movement step over SMB. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Internal Remote Service Port Sweep from One Host
rules.description: Detects one internal host connecting to 20 or more different hosts on remote-service ports (SSH 22, SMB 445, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985) within 10 minutes. This is the recon step attackers run before choosing a service to move with, and it is also how ransomware worms find their next target. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Remote Interactive and Network Logon from Same Unusual Source
rules.description: Detects the same source IP producing both a remote interactive logon (Type 10, RDP-style) and a network logon (Type 3, SMB/WinRM-style) on the same host within 30 minutes. This service-hopping pattern marks attackers mixing tools, not normal users. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Single Source Logons to Multiple Hosts via Remote Services
rules.description: Detects one source IP creating successful logons (network Type 3 or remote interactive Type 10) on 3 or more different hosts within 10 minutes. This fan-out shape fits lateral movement with SMB, WinRM, and RDP, or a worm - it does not fit normal administration from a workstation. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SSH Accepted Public Key from Unusual Source Host
rules.description: Detects a successful SSH login using a public key from a source that is not an approved bastion or admin host. Attackers with a stolen private key need no password, so this line is often the single footprint of the pivot.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Suspicious Remote Service Installation
rules.description: Detects a service installation with a PsExec-style name or a binary path inside an admin share. Attackers copy a small service program into ADMIN$ and start it remotely to run commands as SYSTEM on the target host.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: WinRM Remote Execution with Encoded PowerShell
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks or process creations that use encoded commands (-enc / -EncodedCommand / FromBase64String). Delivered through WinRM, this combination is a strong sign of attacker remote execution.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Enabled via Registry Modification
rules.description: Detects a registry change that turns RDP on (fDenyTSConnections set to 0) or weakens RDP security settings. Malware and hands-on attackers enable RDP to keep a simple way back into a machine.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Fan-Out to Multiple Hosts from One Source
rules.description: Detects one source IP creating RDP sessions on 5 or more different hosts within 24 hours. This shape fits attackers sweeping the network and rare worm behavior, not normal admin work. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Logon from Unusual Source Host
rules.description: Detects an interactive RDP logon (Logon Type 10) from a source IP that is not an approved jump server. Attackers use RDP to move between Windows machines after stealing valid credentials.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Password Guessing Burst
rules.description: Detects 10 or more failed RDP logons (Logon Type 10) from the same source IP within 10 minutes. This pattern shows password guessing or password spraying against exposed or internal RDP. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(IpAddress) >= 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Session Hijack with Tscon
rules.description: Detects tscon.exe called with a /dest: parameter. Attackers with SYSTEM rights use this to redirect another user's active RDP session to their own screen, taking over the session without knowing the password.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Successful Logon After Failed Attempts from Same Source
rules.description: Correlates failed RDP logons (4625) with a successful RDP logon (4624, Type 10) from the same source IP within 30 minutes. This shows a password guess that worked and must be treated as a possible incident. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RDP Tunneling Tool Executed
rules.description: Detects the launch of well-known tunneling tools or any process in a Temp folder using reverse port forwarding. Attackers use these to reach internal RDP through an allowed outbound port.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Security Log Cleared After RDP Activity
rules.description: Detects a cleared Security log (Event 1102). Attackers often clear logs after RDP sessions to hide lateral movement. Correlate this event with the Type 10 logons that came before it on the same host.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Admin Type 3 Logon from Non-Jump Host
rules.description: Detects a network (Type 3) logon by an admin-like account from a host outside the jump server range. Pairs with 5145 admin share access in the SIEM version of this rule.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: Executable or Script Written to ADMIN$ Share
rules.description: Detects executable files written into the hidden ADMIN$ share. Attackers stage tools there before running them with a remote service.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: Impacket-Style Service Names and Command Patterns
rules.description: Detects known impacket executor service names in 7045 and the cmd.exe quiet-mode patterns those tools type into 4688.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: PsExec-Style Remote Service Install
rules.description: Detects the default service name of PsExec and short random service names that remote execution tools create over admin shares.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: Remote Command Execution via WMI Node or Admin Share Path
rules.description: Detects command lines that target remote systems with WMI (/node:) or that reference the hidden ADMIN$ share directly.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: Sensitive Share Access by Unusual User
rules.description: Detects file access (5145) to HR or Finance shares by accounts that are not on the known service account allowlist.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: Share Enumeration Burst from a Single Source
rules.description: Detects one source connecting to the IPC$ share on many hosts within 10 minutes. Tools do this to map which servers expose shares. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Guide

rules.title: Admin Share Access Following Network Logon from Same Host
rules.description: Detects a read of the C$ or ADMIN$ admin share that follows a Type 3 network logon from the same source host within 10 minutes. After DCOM execution, attackers fetch command output or copy tools this way. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DCOM Activation Permission Error (Event 10036)
rules.description: Detects rejected COM activations in the Microsoft-Windows-DCOM Operational log. The message contains the client address. Repeated errors from a host that does not administer the target suggest DCOM probing or lateral movement attempts with wrong permissions.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DCOM Lateral Movement via MMC20.Application (PowerShell 4104)
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that create the MMC20.Application COM object on a remote computer and call ExecuteShellCommand. This is the classic DCOM lateral movement pattern published by enigma0x3 in 2017.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DCOM Lateral Movement via ShellWindows or ShellBrowserWindow (PowerShell 4104)
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that create hidden Explorer COM objects (ShellWindows or ShellBrowserWindow) and call ShellExecute, or that resolve any Shell-named ProgID together with CreateInstance — the DCOM remote execution pattern.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DistributedCOM Permission Settings Events 10016 (Hygiene Baseline)
rules.description: Counts DistributedCOM event 10016 records in the System log. These events fire on almost every default Windows host, so this rule is not an alert. Use it to build the inventory of hosts with wide COM permission settings and to find machines that missed the 2022 DCOM hardening.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Encoded PowerShell Spawned by explorer.exe (Possible DCOM ShellExecute)
rules.description: Detects PowerShell started with an encoded command by explorer.exe. The ShellWindows and ShellBrowserWindow DCOM objects use a hidden Explorer window to ShellExecute programs on the target, so a server showing this pair means a remote activation just ran.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: RPC Endpoint Mapper Sweep to Multiple Hosts
rules.description: Detects a single host connecting to TCP 135 on more than 10 different destinations within 10 minutes. This is RPC/DCOM reconnaissance before lateral movement, not normal administration from a management zone. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Sensitive Access to lsass.exe Memory (Sysmon 10)
rules.description: Detects a process requesting access to lsass.exe with rights that allow reading memory. After a DCOM pivot, attackers dump credential material this way to reach the next hop, often with comsvcs.dll MiniDump.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Shell Spawned by MMC (Possible DCOM ExecuteShellCommand)
rules.description: Detects cmd, powershell, or wscript processes created by mmc.exe. MMC is a graphical console; it does not spawn shells on its own. A remote DCOM ExecuteShellCommand call through MMC20.Application does exactly this.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Direct Root SSH Login Accepted
rules.description: Detects any successful SSH login as root with a key or a password. Hardened baselines set PermitRootLogin no, so every hit is a configuration break or an attacker with direct root access.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: New Key Added to authorized_keys
rules.description: Detects a write to an authorized_keys file that was not made by an approved CI/CD or configuration management account. Attackers add their own public key for persistence (T1098.004) after stealing a first set of credentials.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: One Source Logs Into Many Hosts with Public Keys
rules.description: Detects one source IP and account accepting public key logins on 3 or more distinct destination hosts within 24 hours. This fan-out pattern matches a stolen deploy or admin key used to walk the estate. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Script Execution from Temp Path inside an SSH Session
rules.description: Detects a shell started by sshd that runs a script from /tmp or /dev/shm. This is the staging pattern of ransomware and coin-miner crews that arrive over SSH and execute their payload from a hidden temp folder.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SSH Client Started with Agent Forwarding
rules.description: Detects an ssh process started with the -A (agent forwarding) flag, seen in auditd execve records. Attackers use this flag to reach the next hop with an agent socket that is not theirs, so each hit on a server should be checked.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SSH Password Brute Force Burst
rules.description: Detects 10 or more failed SSH password logons from the same source IP within 10 minutes. This pattern shows password guessing or spraying against exposed or weak-password servers. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) >= 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SSH Public Key Login from Unusual Source Subnet
rules.description: Detects a successful SSH login with a public key whose source IP is not an approved bastion or admin subnet. Stolen keys are usually used from workstations, build servers, or cloud hosts that the account never used.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SSH Tunnel or Port Forward Started from a Server
rules.description: Detects an ssh process with dynamic (-D), remote (-R), local (-L), or tun-interface (-w) forwarding flags. Triage hits on servers first; admins normally run -L only from laptops.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: sshd_config Modified
rules.description: Detects a write to /etc/ssh/sshd_config using the auditd watch with key sshd-config-watch. Changes can enable root login, password login, or weak algorithms, which makes every other SSH attack cheaper.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Inbound VNC Port from Unusual Source
rules.description: Detects an inbound network connection to VNC ports 5900-5906 whose source is not an approved support network. Internet-exposed VNC servers with weak legacy passwords are a common retail and kiosk foothold.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Large Egress After VNC Session
rules.description: Detects a VNC session on port 5900 that moves an unusually large volume of bytes. Remote-control visits that carry a gigabyte are usually setup for collecting and copying data out of stores, kiosks, and file servers. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: New VNC Service Installed
rules.description: Detects the installation of a new Windows service with a VNC-related name. Attackers install VNC as a service for persistent full-desktop access on servers and point-of-sale terminals.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Security Service Stopped After Remote VNC Session
rules.description: Detects a security or antivirus service entering the stopped state. Correlate with an inbound or active session on port 5900 within the timeframe: an attacker controlling the desktop through VNC is the usual reason protection turns off without a change ticket.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: VNC Password Brute Force Indicators
rules.description: Detects 20 or more connections to VNC port 5900 from one source within 10 minutes. Classic VNC authentication has no lockout, so password guessers reconnect in a tight loop and the firewall is the only witness. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) >= 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: VNC Persistence via Registry Run Key
rules.description: Detects a write to a Windows Run autorun key whose stored value references VNC. Rogue VNC servers use Run keys to restart at every login without needing a service or admin rights.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: VNC Server Process from User-Writable Path
rules.description: Detects a VNC-named executable running from a folder users can write to. Attackers drop small VNC servers into Public, Temp, or AppData folders for hidden remote-control access that survives reboots.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Account Created During WinRM Session
rules.description: Detects a user account creation (event 4720) on a host that had a WinRM network logon (event 4624, Type 3, Negotiate) moments earlier. The near operator ties the two events together within the timeframe on the same machine. Attackers create accounts this way to keep access even after the stolen password is reset. On a domain controller the new account is a domain account; on member servers it is a local one. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Encoded PowerShell Command via WinRM
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that carry an encoded command, seen in event 4104 or on the command line in event 4688. Attackers encode payloads with -EncodedCommand or FromBase64String to hide them from plain-text rules. The 4104 event records the decoded content, so the rule leads straight to the payload.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Invoke-Command Fan-Out from Unusual Host
rules.description: Detects PowerShell script blocks that call Invoke-Command with a list of -ComputerName targets from a host that is not an approved jump server. This is one command prepared to hit many servers at once. Hosts outside the approved jump server list are the interesting ones.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: LSASS Memory Dump via comsvcs.dll
rules.description: Detects rundll32 loading comsvcs.dll with the MiniDump export against lsass.exe, or a process opening lsass with read access (Sysmon event 10, GrantedAccess 0x1010). Attackers favor this pair because rundll32 is signed and no dump tool ever lands on disk. Correlate with the WinRM session that carried the command.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Mass WinRM Network Connections from One Source
rules.description: Detects one machine opening WinRM connections (TCP 5985 or 5986) to five or more different targets within ten minutes. This is the network shape of an Invoke-Command sweep across many servers. Check the source against the admin tier before you judge it, because patching tools also fan out. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: WinRM Listener or Service Configuration Change
rules.description: Detects writes to WinRM listener registry keys and changes to the WinRM service configuration key. Attackers enable or modify listeners to keep a remote channel open, or install a service named after WinRM. Pair this rule with event 7045 (new service installed) filtered on WinRM, which the matching SPL query includes.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: WinRM Remote PowerShell Session on Non-Jump Host
rules.description: Detects wsmprovhost.exe, the process that hosts remote PowerShell commands, starting on a machine that is not an approved jump server. The rule also matches its children, because every remote command runs inside it. One hit outside the admin tier is the strongest single sign of WinRM lateral movement.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: AWS CloudTrail Logging Stopped or Trail Deleted
rules.description: Detects attempts to stop or delete CloudTrail logging, including denied attempts blocked by a service control policy. A denied attempt still proves a hostile actor is active inside the account.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: AWS Console Login Without MFA or from New Country
rules.description: Detects successful console logins where MFA was not used (typical for a replayed stolen session cookie) or the login comes from a country outside the expected list. Covers the LAPSUS$ and Scattered Spider access pattern.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: AWS SSM SendCommand by Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects the SendCommand API call made by a principal that is not one of the approved automation roles. Attackers with stolen credentials use SendCommand to run shell commands on virtual machines without any SSH or console login.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: AWS SSM StartSession from Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects SSM Session Manager start events by principals outside the approved bastion and on-call list. A stolen cloud identity can open an interactive shell on private VMs with no SSH key and no network path to the VM.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Bulk S3 Object Read by Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects 1000 or more S3 GetObject events by one principal within 30 minutes, excluding known backup roles. Matches the bulk exfiltration pattern of the 2024 stolen-credential data theft campaigns. Requires S3 data events. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(userIdentity.arn) >= 1000 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: New IAM Access Key Created and Used Within One Hour
rules.description: Correlates an IAM CreateAccessKey event with follow-up API activity by the same principal within one hour. Shows a freshly minted key that is already being used - the persistence step seen in cloud intrusion campaigns. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Rare Cloud API Enumeration Burst by One Principal
rules.description: Detects a single principal calling 50 or more distinct Describe*, List*, or Get* event names within 15 minutes. Shows programmatic enumeration of the account, which usually precedes execution or exfiltration steps. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: AWS EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint Created
rules.description: Detects the creation of an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint. This API is a direct change to the private network path of a VPC and is rare in most accounts. Attackers who hold a valid IAM role use it to reach private VMs without a public IP or VPN.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: AWS EC2 Serial Console SSH Public Key Sent
rules.description: Detects a key push for the EC2 Serial Console. The serial console is a root-level recovery door that works even when networking is broken, so any use deserves a page to a human.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Instance Connect Endpoint Deleted and Recreated Within 24h
rules.description: Aggregation rule: the same principal or account deletes an Instance Connect Endpoint and creates a new one within 24 hours. Attackers rotate endpoints to escape temporary reach or to mimic cleanup. Approved pipelines do this on schedule, so group by identity and compare against the change calendar.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Process After Instance Connect Session
rules.description: Detects an ssh process started with a reverse tunnel flag (-R) on a Linux instance, which is a common way for attackers to call home after gaining a shell through Instance Connect. For environments without endpoint telemetry, watch netflow for long-lived high-byte outbound sessions right after a SendSSHPublicKey event.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SendSSHPublicKey by Machine Identity Without Recent ConsoleLogin
rules.description: Detects a temporary SSH key push by a machine identity (userIdentity.type AssumedRole, the identity a program or role session uses). Humans normally log in to the console first; robot roles should not behave like people. The classic rule below matches the machine-identity part. The Splunk search adds the true 24-hour ConsoleLogin lookback with a subsearch.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SendSSHPublicKey by Unusual Principal
rules.description: Detects a temporary SSH key being pushed to an EC2 instance by a principal that is not on the approved admin or pipeline allow list. A leaked CI/CD role calling this API is a strong sign of direct cloud VM access abuse.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: SSH Login Marked ec2-instance-connect with Unknown Key Fingerprint
rules.description: Detects an accepted SSH login on a Linux instance whose auth log message contains the provider marker ec2-instance-connect, where the key fingerprint is not one of the approved admin fingerprints. This is where the cloud event becomes a real session on the machine.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: PowerShell Download Cradle with Invoke-Expression
rules.description: Detects PowerShell processes combining download methods with expression invocation, typical of download-and-execute cradles used to fetch second-stage payloads.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Many Special-Privilege Logons for One Account in 10 Minutes
rules.description: An account collecting special privileges on many hosts in a short window often means stolen-token movement between systems. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: NewCredentials Logon (Type 9) with runas
rules.description: Logon type 9 means Windows received new credentials for the session. The normal source is runas /netonly, which attackers also abuse to act under another identity without a new interactive logon.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: Process from a User Folder Opens LSASS
rules.description: On a home PC, almost no legitimate program in a user-writable folder has a reason to open LSASS. Every hit deserves a check.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: SeDebugPrivilege Enabled Through a Token Right Adjustment
rules.description: Event 4700 records a token right adjustment. SeDebugPrivilege allows opening protected processes, which credential and token theft tools need.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: Service Account Signs In from Two Countries in One Hour
rules.description: A stolen cloud token is often replayed from another country or a hosting service. Watch for one account with successful sign-ins from more than one country in a short window. Field names follow the Microsoft Entra sign-in schema; adjust them to your table. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: Suspicious Read Access to LSASS Memory
rules.description: A process opens lsass.exe with access rights that allow reading its memory. Tools that dump credentials or steal tokens need this first.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: SYSTEM Script Host Spawned by the Service Manager
rules.description: services.exe starting cmd, PowerShell, or script hosts as SYSTEM is a common pattern in service and token abuse chains. Known management agents must be filtered.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: Token Impersonation Tooling on the Command Line
rules.description: Well-known red-team and admin tooling for stealing or making Windows access tokens appears in a process command line.
rules.author: T1134.001 detection guide

rules.title: Cloud CLI Token Cache Copied or Archived
rules.description: An archiving, copy, or shell command touches local token caches and secret files of cloud CLIs (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, SSH). Infostealers and hands-on attackers grab these files to reuse valid tokens (T1528.001).
rules.author: T1528 Detection Guide

rules.title: Non-Browser Process Touches Browser Cookie Store
rules.description: A process that is not a web browser creates or writes to the cookie database of Chrome, Edge, or Firefox. Malware and infostealers do this to copy web session cookies and reuse them on another machine (T1528.004).
rules.author: T1528 Detection Guide

rules.title: Pentest Tool User Agent in AWS Security Token Service Calls
rules.description: AWS STS token calls (AssumeRole, GetSessionToken, GetFederationToken) arrive with a user agent that belongs to attack or scan tools. This often means someone is replaying or testing stolen AWS credentials or tokens (T1528.001).
rules.author: T1528 Detection Guide

rules.title: Stolen Okta Session - Same User From Several IP Addresses
rules.description: One Okta user completes SSO from more than one IP address inside a short time window. This can mean that a session token was stolen and replayed from another machine (T1528.004). Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: T1528 Detection Guide

rules.title: Successful Device Code Sign-In From Unusual Country
rules.description: A sign-in completed with the device code flow from a country your users do not use. Attackers phish employees into entering a device code so that the attacker receives a valid OAuth token (T1528.003).
rules.author: T1528 Detection Guide

rules.title: Possible Stolen Refresh Token - Non-Interactive Sign-In From New Country
rules.description: A non-interactive sign-in (refresh token or cached token) succeeded from a country that your users do not normally use, with no second factor. This is a common pattern when an attacker replays a stolen token.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Golden SAML Preparation - ADFS Certificate Dump or Export Tools
rules.description: Someone runs known tools or commands used to read or export the AD FS token-signing certificate and its keys. With this certificate an attacker can forge SAML tokens for any user (T1528.002, Golden SAML).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Risky OAuth Application Consent Grant
rules.description: A user consented to an OAuth application that asks for risky mail or file permissions. Consent phishing gives the attacker a valid token without a password. Covers MITRE ATT&CK T1528.003 (OAuth Token).
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: Delivered Inbound Reply-Style Message (Hunt for Unknown Sender Domains)
rules.description: Detects inbound delivered mail whose subject starts with RE: or FW: for analyst review. The rule itself does not check the sender, so join it with your partner-domain list to surface messages whose sender domain is not a known partner. Thread hijacking hides phishing links inside real conversations; the subject style and the new domain together break the illusion.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: High Volume Inbound SMTP Connection Wave from One Source
rules.description: Detects a burst of inbound SMTP connections from a single source within five minutes on a Postfix relay. Malspam campaigns produce this pattern before any filter learns the campaign. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Mobile Device Opens Parcel or Pickup Themed Link
rules.description: Detects a corporate device fetching a parcel, pickup, or delivery themed page from a mobile browser. Smishing campaigns use these exact words to move staff off email and onto phones.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Mobile User Agent Reaches Look-Alike Login Page
rules.description: Detects a mobile browser opening a login-shaped page on a host that mimics Microsoft-style sign-in naming but is not Microsoft. QR-code phishing pushes victims to exactly this flow on their phones.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Office Application Spawning Command Interpreter
rules.description: Detects Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or Outlook starting powershell, cmd, mshta, or the Windows Script Host. This is the classic macro phishing execution pattern (T1566.001 followed by user execution).
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Office or Mail Client Writes Disk Image or Script Container
rules.description: Detects Outlook or Office applications creating ISO, IMG, LNK, HTA, or CHM files on disk. Attackers wrap payloads in these containers to slip past macro blocks; a mail client has no reason to produce them.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Okta MFA Factor Reset or Deactivation
rules.description: Detects a successful reset or deactivation of a multi-factor factor in Okta. Vishing attackers call the help desk, ask for this reset, and enroll their own device minutes later. Join with the following enrollment event for high confidence.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Remote Access Tool Started from a User-Writable Folder
rules.description: Detects AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ScreenConnect, RemoteUtilities, or Atera starting from Temp, Downloads, or AppData. Callback phishing operators talk victims into running these tools; managed deployments come from Program Files.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Successful High-Risk Sign-In (Password Replay Pattern)
rules.description: Detects a successful sign-in that Microsoft Entra ID scored as high risk. Credential replay from a phishing kit or an anonymizing network usually arrives as a password-only, single-factor sign-in from a new network; enrich the alert by checking authenticationDetails for a lone Password entry and authenticationRequirement for singleFactorAuthentication.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: User Consents to OAuth Application with Mail Scope
rules.description: Detects a user-level OAuth consent grant in the Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log. Consent phishing needs exactly this event; scopes with Mail.Read and offline_access hand the attacker a lasting token.
rules.author: Detection Guide Team

rules.title: Email Delivered with a Risky Attachment File Type
rules.description:
Detects inbound email carrying historically abused attachment types
(disk images, macro documents, OneNote, shortcuts). Field names follow
Defender for Office 365 (EmailAttachmentInfo): FileName, DeliveryAction,
SenderAddress, RecipientAddress, Subject. For other gateways (Proofpoint,
Mimecast, Barracuda), map these five fields once in your ingest pipeline.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Microsoft Office for macOS Spawned a Script Interpreter or Download Tool
rules.description:
Detects Microsoft Office applications on macOS starting shells,
scripting tools, or downloaders - the macOS version of macro payload
execution after a phishing attachment (T1566.001).
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: MS Office Application Spawned a Script or Shell Interpreter
rules.description:
Detects a Microsoft Office application starting a command line or script
interpreter. Strong sign that a macro or exploit inside an email
attachment (T1566.001) is executing attacker code.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Office-Descendant Process Created Run Key or Startup Persistence
rules.description:
Detects Office applications or PowerShell writing to autostart
registry locations. Malware from a phishing attachment (T1566.001)
survives reboots this way (T1547.001).
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Office or PowerShell Process Opened an External Network Connection
rules.description:
Detects Office applications or PowerShell initiating outbound network
connections to non-private addresses. Payload download (T1105) and C2
beaconing (T1071.001) after a spearphishing attachment (T1566.001)
both look like this.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Office Process Dropped an Executable or Script into a Temp Folder
rules.description:
Detects Microsoft Office applications writing executable or script
files into user-writable temp directories - payload staging after a
malicious attachment (T1566.001).
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: One Sender Domain Sent Attachments to Many Users
rules.description:
Trend rule for mass attachment campaigns (precursor to T1566.001).
Uses Sigma aggregation: count inbound mails with attachments per
sender domain and alert above a threshold. The SenderDomain field must
exist in your logs (most gateways add it; in Splunk we derive it from
SenderAddress with eval - see the SPL below). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(SenderDomain) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawned by Outlook or Office
rules.description: Detects Office and Outlook applications spawning script or shell child processes, a common follow-up behavior after a user opens a malicious spearphishing attachment.
rules.author: Souhaieb Marzouk

rules.title: PowerShell Download Cradle or Encoded Execution in Command Line
rules.description:
Detects PowerShell fetching and running remote content, or certutil
used as a downloader. Common second stage after a malicious email
attachment (T1566.001).
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Suspicious Process Execution from a Linux Mail or Temp Directory
rules.description:
Implements the Linux part of the official ATT&CK analytic AN0656:
links email delivery to later process execution from mail directories.
Works with Sysmon for Linux, osquery process_events, or any Linux EDR
that fills the process_creation fields.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Windows Defender Detected Malware After an Email Attachment
rules.description:
Aggregates Microsoft Defender malware detection events. Blocked is not
safe: campaigns retry with new variants, so every detection after a
phishing wave (T1566.001) needs human review.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Banner Grab Burst on Service Ports
rules.description: One external source opens many short TCP connections to service ports, transfers zero bytes, and ends each one with a reset. This is the typical shape of banner grabbing and service fingerprinting before an attack (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 40 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DNS Probing of Infrastructure Subdomains
rules.description: One external source asks the public DNS server for many infrastructure subdomains such as vpn, mail, owa, and autodiscover in a short time. This is a classic sign of DNS-based network reconnaissance (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: External Port Scan Burst Against Public Range
rules.description: Many blocked inbound connections to public-facing hosts from one external source in a short window. This pattern often appears during pre-attack network reconnaissance, when an intruder maps open services before an intrusion (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 30 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Recon Burst from Hosting or VPN Provider Ranges
rules.description: Denied inbound traffic from source addresses inside known hosting or VPN provider ranges, counted per source in a short window. Attackers rent such exits so their sources look like normal users (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Replace the placeholder documentation ranges in selection_range with the ranges from your enriched threat feed. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Single Source Probing Many Paths on OWA or Admin Portals
rules.description: One external source requests many different paths under mail and admin portals such as /owa, /ecp, /autodiscover, and /admin in a short window. This path walk often precedes exploitation of public-facing servers (MITRE ATT&CK T1590). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(c-ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DNS NXDOMAIN Burst from One Source
rules.description: Counts NXDOMAIN answers per external source in a five-minute window on Zeek dns.log data. A wave of misses from one address is the classic shape of a wordlist enumeration run. This covers threat 5 of section 5.3, bulk mapping. Tune the threshold of 40 to sit just above your measured normal noise. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 40 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DNS Wordlist and Canary Subdomain Probing
rules.description: Detects a source asking for common service names such as vpn, mail, staging or test under the victim domain, or any query for the canary subdomain. This covers threat 2 of section 5.3, hidden portal discovery. A canary hit alone is a strong recon signal with almost no noise. Adjust the name list to your zone. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DNS Zone Transfer Attempt
rules.description: Detects AXFR zone transfer attempts in name server logs. An outside AXFR asks for a copy of the whole zone in one request, which is reconnaissance of the full record set. This covers threat 3 of section 5.3. Allowlist approved secondaries by address before enabling alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Lookalike Domain Resolution Inside the Network
rules.description: Detects Sysmon Event ID 22 DNS queries where the requested name matches known lookalike patterns for the brand. A resolution from inside the network often means a phishing click on a lookalike domain. This covers threat 1 of section 5.3. Update the pattern list from brand monitoring.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Office 365 Tenant Enumeration via Autodiscover or GetUserRealm
rules.description: Detects one external client sending several requests to autodiscover or GetUserRealm paths on mail-facing web servers. Public API endpoints can confirm cloud use and reveal tenant names without any login. This covers threat 4 of section 5.3. Tune the threshold after a week of baseline data. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(client_ip) > 5 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: DNS Zone Transfer (AXFR) Attempt
rules.description: Detects attempts to perform a DNS zone transfer (AXFR) against an authoritative name server. A successful transfer hands the attacker the full list of records of the zone, so every attempt is worth an alert.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: High-Volume Unique-Query Enumeration of a Zone
rules.description: Detects a single source asking for an unusually high number of unique names under one zone in a short window. This is the pattern of broad record sweeps that map a zone and its cloud vendors. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 100 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Reverse DNS (PTR) Sweep
rules.description: Detects a single source issuing many PTR queries in a short window. Walking PTR records across an address block maps server names without touching any system directly. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 30 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Sensitive Subdomain Name Probing
rules.description: Detects a single external source probing several short, sensitive names such as vpn., mail., citrix., jira., or staging. under the victim zone. The attacker is building a list of remote access doors. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 15 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Subdomain Brute Force (NXDOMAIN Storm)
rules.description: Detects a single source receiving many NXDOMAIN answers for names under one zone in a short window. Attackers brute forcing subdomains produce exactly this pattern, because most guessed names do not exist. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 60 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Activity Spike for Guest or External Accounts
rules.description: Detects many network logons (type 3) for one external, guest, or vendor account within one hour. A burst can mean an attacker is walking the trust path with a shared account. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(TargetUserName) > 15 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Cloud SSO Sign-In from External Identity in a New Country
rules.description: Detects a successful cloud SSO sign-in for an external vendor identity from a country that is not on the approved list, often from a new device. Vendor support accounts should sign in only from known places.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Remote Management Tool Connection from a Server Segment
rules.description: Detects a server in the data center range talking to a remote monitoring and management (RMM) service such as AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk, or Splashtop. Intrusion groups abuse these trusted admin tools after mapping vendor trust.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Repeated Calls to a Vendor Update Endpoint from an Unexpected Server
rules.description: Detects many HTTP calls to a vendor update path from one source in a short window. A trusted update channel that repeats on a fixed schedule can hide a beacon from a trojanized update. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 12 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Vendor or Service VPN Login from Unlisted Source IP
rules.description: Detects a vendor or service account logging in to the VPN or firewall from a source IP outside the approved vendor egress pool. This is the classic sign that a trust dependency credential was stolen and is being used.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Edge and VPN Portal Probing
rules.description: Detects one source requesting many VPN, webmail, or admin portal paths on public web servers within ten minutes. This is how an attacker profiles a discovered portal before trying credentials against it. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(clientip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Horizontal Sweep Across External Range
rules.description: Detects a single external source denied on many different destination IPs at the firewall boundary in a short window. This is the classic echo of topology mapping before an intrusion. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Internal Mapping with Built-in Windows Tools
rules.description: Detects bursts of nltest, net view, and nbtstat launches on Windows servers. These commands map domains, shares, and NetBIOS names from inside. This is the post-compromise mapping stage, which MITRE tracks under the Discovery tactic. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(User) > 3 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Traceroute Sweep Through UDP High Ports
rules.description: Detects bursts of UDP probes from one external source to the classic traceroute ports (33434 and above). Zeek logs the probes as short connections with no service. Extend the port list if your sensors see other traceroute styles, such as ICMP-based probes. Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Vertical Scan on Single Host
rules.description: Detects one external source denied on many ports of one destination host. This shows the attacker profiling a specific system, often the VPN gateway or a DMZ host. Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Banner Grabbing Pattern on Management Services
rules.description: Detects many short connections that open a management port, receive a small answer and close at once (Zeek connection state RSTO). This is how attackers grab banners from services they found in the range (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Direct-IP Access Bypassing DNS on Public Web Server
rules.description: Detects web requests where the Host header holds a raw IP address instead of a domain name. This shows that a client found the server address and connected directly, skipping DNS and any CDN protection (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(client_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: One External Source Sweeping Many Victim Addresses
rules.description: Detects one external source contacting more than 15 distinct destination IP addresses within five minutes in the connection states S0 or REJ. Wide sweeps of a whole address block are a classic preparation step before active scanning and initial access (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: apply the SIEM aggregation described in tests/sigma_cases/thresholds.json before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: PTR Reverse Sweep Against the Victim Network
rules.description: Detects a burst of reverse DNS (PTR) lookups for addresses inside the victim in-addr.arpa zone. Attackers sweep PTR records to map address blocks to hostnames while staying quiet (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Remote Access and Management Port Probe Burst
rules.description: Detects one external source sending many denied probes to remote access and management ports such as SSH (22), VPN (1194) and RDP (3389). Attackers use this to find remote access doors inside a scanned range (MITRE ATT&CK T1590.005). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Known-CVE Path Probing on VPN Appliance
rules.description: Detects requests for URI paths tied to published edge appliance CVEs, such as path traversal tricks that leak credentials (T1590.006).
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Management Port Sweep across Edge Appliances
rules.description: Detects one source touching management ports (22, 23, 443, 8443) on several edge appliances in a short window (T1590.006).
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: Repeated TLS Handshakes without Application Data
rules.description: Detects one source opening many TLS sessions to edge appliances with almost no payload, typical for banner and version probing (T1590.006). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(id.orig_h) > 20 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: VPN Admin Portal Probing from One External Source
rules.description: Detects one external source requesting many known VPN admin portal paths in a short window, a classic appliance fingerprinting step (T1590.006). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(client_ip) > 10 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team

rules.title: VPN Portal Credential Stuffing Burst
rules.description: Detects many failed VPN logins from one source in a short window, the follow-up step after leaked or guessed appliance credentials (T1590.006). Detection note: this is the event-level half. Apply the SIEM threshold count(src_ip) > 5 within 5m before alerting.
rules.author: Detection Engineering Team
